notes_for_editor: Thin on newspapers and none searched (Chronicling America search timed out); no NRHP text (PDF not digitised). Disagreements stated in text: parcel size (22 vs nearly 27 acres), completion date (12 vs 23 Nov 1896), towline cut (NOAA) vs broke (society, LF), Fay destination (Ashtabula per society, Cleveland per NOAA, not in story). Not in story: society says first recommendation 1889, LF says 1890. Roster differences: Hanson assistant '-1950' (USLHS) vs 'at least 1950' (LF); Marken 1951-52 (USLHS) vs 1952-55 (LF); Metivier spelled Joseph Metivier in LF. Lens: LF says original Sautter fourth-order and Henry-Lepaute today; society says Lepaute collar dated 1872 and probably third or fourth lens in tower; the 1919 and 1914 changes (LF only) left out. Wikipedia and 1914 Bulletin illuminant-change mention not used. The 1896-97 table entry (cite 9) matched by OCR text, page not determined. Tower height 15.8 m is 52 ft converted; the record says 16.0 m. Fact-check 2026-10-22: seven-mile road distance (society) vs six miles (LF) now stated; NOAA lifeboat account vs society pilot-house account added; LF 1919 lens added.
